newsitem.title: HONG KONG: StanChart's Hong Kong unit upbeat on 1997.
newsitem.headline: StanChart's Hong Kong unit upbeat on 1997.

text.p: Standard Chartered Plc's wholly owned Hong Kong subsidiary Standard Chartered Bank (SCB) said on Wednesday it expects a good year for the territory's banking industry.

David Brougham, group executive director at SCB, told a news conference the local unit achieved record results in 1996, posting a 25 percent increase to HK$3.8 billion. Trading profits grew 22 percent to HK$3.6 billion.

The Hong Kong arm's operating profit improved to 3.1 percent from 2.8 percent while the cost-to-income ratio fell to 46 percent from 51 percent in 1996, he said. Net interest income rose 16 percent to HK$5.1 billion during the year.
However, charges for debts rose 100 percent to HK$200 million last year. Brougham said the 1996 level was not high, and attributed the increase to an exceptionally low figure in 1995.
Brougham said Hong Kong's banking industry experienced a difficult year in 1996 in part due to a highly competitive mortgage market and weak exports but said he saw improvements ahead in 1997.
"I believe that it is a good year for Hong Kong and should be a good year for banking," he said. "We'll expect a strong economy."
Ian Wilson, the bank's general manager for Hong Kong, China and Northeast Asia, said he expected mortgage and trade finance-related businesses in particular to perform well.
Asked if SCB would seek a Hong Kong-listing, Brougham said "I think that is highly unlikely."
